'''Milton Diamond''' (March 6, 1934<ref name=":0" /> – March 20, 2024) was an American professor of [[anatomy]] and [[reproductive biology]] at the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa]].<ref name=emer>{{cite web| url=http://www.hawaii.edu/offices/bor/regular/notice/201409250900.regular.pdf | publisher= University of Hawaiʻi | title= Board of Regents' Meeting, Thursday, September 25, 2014 | access-date = February 8, 2015}}</ref> After a career in the study of [[human sexuality]], Diamond retired from the university in December 2009 but continued with his research and writing until retiring fully in 2018.<ref name=retired>{{cite web| url=http://www.hawaii.edu/PCSS/ | publisher= University of Hawaiʻi | title= Pacific Center for Sex and Society – Home Page | access-date = January 21, 2020}}</ref>  He died on March 20, 2024, at the age of 90.<ref name=pcssobit>{{cite web| url=http://www.hawaii.edu/PCSS/obituary/index.html | publisher= University of Hawaii | title= Obituary - Professor Emeritus Milton Diamond Ph.D. | access-date = March 22, 2024}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Risen |first=Clay |date=2024-05-08 |title=Milton Diamond, Sexologist and Advocate for Intersex Babies, Dies at 90 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/08/health/milton-diamond-dead.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240508201125/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/08/health/milton-diamond-dead.html |archive-date=May 8, 2024 |access-date=2024-07-23 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Early career==
Milton Diamond graduated from the [[City College of New York]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] in [[biophysics]] in 1955,<ref name=sab /><ref name=":0" /> after which he spent three years in the [[United States Army|Army]] as an engineering officer, stationed in Japan.<ref name=ca /> On returning to the United States, he attended graduate school at [[University of Kansas]] from 1958 to 1962 where he earned a [[PhD]] in anatomy and [[psychology]].<ref name=ca>{{cite web| url=http://www.changelingaspects.com/Technical/Prof%20M%20Diamond-bio.htm | publisher= Changeling Aspects | title= An Introduction to Professor Milton Diamond Ph.D. | access-date = September 16, 2009}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> His first job was teaching at the [[University of Louisville]], School of Medicine where he simultaneously completed two years toward a [[Doctor of Medicine]], passing his Basic Medicine Boards,<ref name=sab /> and in 1967 he moved to Hawaii to take up a post at the recently established [[John A. Burns School of Medicine]].

Milton Diamond had a long running feud with the psychologist Dr. [[John Money]]. In 1965 Diamond published ''A Critical Evaluation of the Ontogeny of Human Sexual Behavior'',<ref>''A Critical Evaluation of the Ontogeny of Human Sexual Behavior'' [https://booksc.eu/book/23641176/476425]</ref> a critique of Money's work. In the early seventies, Diamond and Money were attending a conference on transgenderism in [[Dubrovnik]]. According to the book ''[[As Nature Made Him: The Boy Who Was Raised as a Girl]]'' (page 174),<ref name="Colapintobook">[[Colapinto, John]] (2000). ''[[As Nature Made Him: The Boy Who Was Raised as a Girl]].'' HarperCollins. {{ISBN|0-06-092959-6}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> at this conference Money initiated a loud and aggressive argument with Diamond. Eyewitnesses claimed Money punched Diamond; however, Diamond himself said that he could not recall any physical contact during this encounter.<ref name=":0" />

==David Reimer==
Diamond was best known for following up on the case of [[David Reimer]], a boy raised as a girl under the supervision of [[John Money]] after his penis was damaged beyond surgical repair during a botched [[circumcision]], which was performed using an unconventional method of [[electrocauterization]] instead of a clamp and scalpel.<ref>{{cite book |last=Colapinto |first=John |author-link=John Colapinto |year=2001|title=As Nature Made Him: The Boy Who Was Raised as a Girl|url=https://archive.org/details/asnaturemadehim00john |url-access=registration |location=New York|publisher=HarperCollins|isbn=978-0-06-019211-2
|pages=[https://archive.org/details/asnaturemadehim00john/page/11 11-13]}}</ref><ref name=BBCHealthCheck>{{cite news |date=November 23, 2010 |title=Health Check: The Boy Who Was Raised a Girl |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-11814300 |publisher=BBC News |access-date=December 19, 2014}}</ref> This case, which Money renamed that of "John/Joan" to protect Reimer's privacy, has become one of the most cited cases in the literature of [[psychiatry]], [[anthropology]], [[women's studies]], [[child development]], and [[biology of gender]].{{citation needed|date=September 2014}} With the cooperation of H. Keith Sigmundson, who had been Reimer's supervising psychiatrist, Diamond tracked down the adult Reimer and found that Money's sex reassignment of Reimer had failed. Diamond was the first to alert physicians that the model, proposed by Reimer's case, of how to treat infants with [[intersex]] conditions was faulty.<ref name="si">{{cite web| url= http://www.hawaii.edu/PCSS/biblio/articles/1961to1999/1982-sexual-identity.html | publisher= Milton Diamond, Ph.D | title= Sexual Identity, Monozygotic Twins Reared in Discordant Sex Roles and a BBC Follow-Up | access-date = August 1, 2011}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> 

Diamond recommended<ref name="moi">{{cite journal|last=Diamond|first=Milton|author2=Sigmundson, H. Keith|title=Management of intersexuality. Guidelines for dealing with persons with ambiguous genitalia.|journal=Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med|date=October 1997|volume=151|issue=10|pages=1046–50|doi=10.1001/archpedi.1997.02170470080015|pmid=9343018|url=http://www.hawaii.edu/PCSS/biblio/articles/1961to1999/1997-management-of-intersexuality.html|access-date=April 24, 2013|url-access=subscription}}</ref> that physicians should not perform surgery on intersex people without their informed consent,<ref name=":0" /> should assign such infants to the gender to which they will probably best adjust, and refrain from adding shame, stigma and secrecy to the issue, by assisting intersex people to meet and associate with others of like condition. Diamond similarly encouraged considering the intersex condition as a difference of sex development, not as a [[Disorders of sex development|disorder]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Diamond |first1=Milton |last2=Beh |first2=Hazel. |year=2008 |title=Changes In Management Of Children With Differences Of Sex Development. |journal=Nature Clinical Practice Endocrinology & Metabolism |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=4–5|doi=10.1038/ncpendmet0694 |pmid=17984980 |hdl=10125/66380 |s2cid=13382948 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>

==Work, appointments and awards==
Diamond wrote extensively about [[abortion]] and [[family planning]], [[pornography]], [[intersexuality]], [[transsexuality]], and other sex- and [[reproduction]]-related issues for sex-related scientific journals as well as legal journals. He also wrote for lay periodicals. He was frequently interviewed for public media and legal matters, and often served as an expert in court proceedings, and was known for his research on the origins and development of [[sexual identity]]. He retired from teaching in 2009, but continued to research and consult concerning transsexuality, intersexuality and pornography until he retired fully in 2018.

===Appointments===
Diamond was based at the John A. Burns School of Medicine at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, from 1967.<ref name=ca /> He was appointed Professor of Anatomy and Reproductive Biology in 1971, and from 1985 until his retirement he was Director of the Pacific Center for Sex and Society<ref name=ca /> within the School of Medicine.

In 1999 Diamond was appointed President of the [[International Academy of Sex Research]],<ref name=iasr>{{cite web | url= http://www.iasr.org/node/1 | publisher= International Academy of Sex Research | title= Meeting History | access-date= September 15, 2009 | url-status= usurped | archive-url= https://archive.today/20090330172938/http://www.iasr.org/node/1 | archive-date= March 30, 2009}}</ref> and in 2001/02 President of the [[Society for the Scientific Study of Sexuality]].<ref name=sss>{{cite web | url= http://www.sexscience.org/about/index.php?category_id=1182 | publisher= The Society for the Scientific Study of Sexuality | title= Society Presidents | access-date= September 15, 2009 | url-status= dead | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20091115181404/http://www.sexscience.org/about/index.php?category_id=1182 | archive-date= November 15, 2009}}</ref>

===Awards===
The awards Diamond received include:
*1999: the British GIRES Research Prize<ref name=gires>{{cite web | url= http://www.gires.org.uk/awards1999.php | publisher= Gender Identity Research and Education Society | title= Past awards for research | access-date= November 24, 2010 | url-status= dead | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110718115954/http://www.gires.org.uk/awards1999.php | archive-date= July 18, 2011}}</ref>
*2000: the German [[Magnus Hirschfeld Medal]] for sexual science<ref name=magnus>{{cite web | url= http://www2.hu-berlin.de/sexology/GESUND/ARCHIV/LAUDA.HTM | publisher= HUMBOLDT-UNIVERSITÄT ZU BERLIN | title= Archive for Sexology | access-date= November 11, 2009 | url-status= dead | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090901071735/http://www2.hu-berlin.de/sexology/GESUND/ARCHIV/LAUDA.HTM | archive-date= September 1, 2009}}</ref>
*2005: the Norwegian Diversity Prize for his research efforts on behalf of [[transsexual]] and [[transgender]] people worldwide
*2008: the first of a proposed annual award made by the German Intersex Society (Intersexuelle Menschen e.V.)<ref name=gis>{{cite web| url=http://www.intersexuelle-menschen.net | title=Intersexuelle Menschen e.V. | access-date = September 15, 2009}}</ref> "for his decades-long commitment to the benefit of [[intersex]] people";<ref name=gis2>{{cite web | url=http://www.intersexuelle-menschen.net/IMEVzusatz/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=2&Itemid=3 | publisher=Zwischengeschlecht.info | title=Zwischengeschlechtliche ehrten Milton Diamond | access-date=September 15, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090920150249/http://www.intersexuelle-menschen.net/IMEVzusatz/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=2&Itemid=3 | archive-date=September 20, 2009}}</ref>
*2009: the Regents' Medal for Excellence in Research by the University of Hawaiʻi;<ref name=uhnews>{{cite web| url=http://www.hawaii.edu/news/article.php?aId=3055 | publisher= University of Hawaiʻi System | title= Regents' Medal for Excellence in Research awarded to outstanding UH faculty | access-date = September 15, 2009}}</ref>
*2010: the Kinsey Award for 2011, made by the Midcontinent Region of the [[Society for the Scientific Study of Sexuality]].<ref name=pcss>{{cite web | url= http://www.sexscience.org/honors/kinsey_award/ | publisher= The Society for the Scientific Study of Sexuality | title= Kinsey Award | access-date= August 1, 2011 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110809025020/http://www.sexscience.org/honors/kinsey_award/ | archive-date= August 9, 2011 | url-status= dead}}</ref>
*2015: the [[World Association for Sexual Health]] gold medal<ref name=was>{{cite web| url=http://www.worldsexology.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/WAS-NEWSLETTER-JUNE-2015-IN-ENGLISH.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005042233/http://www.worldsexology.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/WAS-NEWSLETTER-JUNE-2015-IN-ENGLISH.pdf | url-status=usurped | archive-date=October 5, 2015 | publisher= The World Association for Sexual Health | title= WAS Newsletter 2015, Volume 12 Issue 1 | access-date = October 4, 2015}}</ref>
*2025: Posthumously awarded by [[InterACT]]: the 2024 Anne Tamar-Mattis Advocacy Award.<ref name=atm> {{cite web| url=https://interactadvocates.org/atm-intersex-advocacy-award/ | publisher = InterACT | title=Anne Tamar-Mattis Advocacy Award for Intersex Allyship |access-date=March 5, 2025}}</ref>
